Command: Remove the Unclean from the Camp
Summary: Command the children of Israel, that they put out of the camp every leper, and every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead — male and female alike. This Numbers 5 camp rule is distinct from the live Purity row, whose range is Leviticus 12-15.
Commandment: Put outside the camp every leper, everyone with a discharge, and everyone defiled by the dead, until cleansed.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The camp was where God dwelt among his people, so uncleanness was kept outside it until cleansed. The New Testament reverses the direction: Jesus touches the leper and the unclean are brought in, not sent out (Mark 1:40-45; Luke 8:43-48, both cited on the live Purity row) — which is why this camp rule is temporary, not continuing.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: that they defile not their camps, in the midst whereof I dwell (Numbers 5:3).
